beats.care: Missions like this show where space science jobs are heading. ISRO and India's space startups are chasing the same kind of sample-return skills.
beats.what: Japan's space agency JAXA launched the Martian Moons eXploration mission on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima on 20 October, Japan time.
beats.why: Scientists don't know if Mars's two small moons are captured asteroids or debris from a giant crash into Mars.

cards.body: A small four-wheeled rover called IDEFIX, built by France and Germany, will scout Phobos's surface for up to 100 hours. NASA supplied a sampler and a science instrument, and gets at least 15% of the sample.
If Phobos is a chunk knocked off Mars, its rock holds clues about early Mars. If it is a captured asteroid, it tells us how material moved around the young solar system.

tldr: Japan launched MMX, a spacecraft that will land on Mars's moon Phobos and bring a sample back to Earth by 2031.
watch: MMX reaches Mars in August 2027 and aims to land on Phobos from December 2028. Samples land in Australia in 2031.
